concepts.definition: a substance in food that the body needs for energy, growth, repair, or regulation
a nutrient that is a major source of energy for the body
a nutrient made of amino acids that supports growth, repair, and many body functions
an energy-dense nutrient that also supports insulation, cell structure, and vitamin absorption
an organic micronutrient required in small amounts for normal growth and metabolism
an inorganic nutrient needed in small amounts for structural and regulatory body functions
a diet that supplies appropriate amounts of nutrients and energy for a person's needs
methods used to slow spoilage and extend the safe storage life of food
practices that keep food, equipment, and handlers clean enough to reduce contamination
the organized selection of meals to meet nutritional, financial, cultural, and practical needs
